newsitem.title: SPAIN: Wall St helps Madrid stocks up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Wall St helps Madrid stocks up in thin trade.

text.p: Madrid stocks closed higher on Monday helped by gains on Wall Street and in bonds.
But trade was thin and dull awaiting domestic and U.S. inflation on Friday, as well as concrete details on the new government's 1997 budget.
The general index up 1.73 points, 0.50 percent, to 350.89 and the Ibex rose 24.81 points, 0.63 percent, to 3,987.88.

Repsol dropped 30 pesetas to 4,080 after announcing a cut of up to two pesetas per litre in petrol prices to the public. The news was considered slightly negative for the oil stock, but saw an exaggerated move in thin trade, a dealer said.
Gas Natural rebounded from last week's lows prompted by news of a lower than expected tariff hike. It rose 370 pesetas to 20,760.
Many are awaiting the inflation data, which is limiting trading volumes. Meanwhile the market is content to track other bourses.
"We've followed a tune marked abroad, but without final investors in a market dominated by traders and with no clear trend defined short-term," said one fund manager.
Volume totalled a paltry 17.5 billion pesetas.
